selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What two ideas does the passage say mercy shows at the same time?
questions.answer: It shows Allah’s unity and His oneness within that unity.

questions.question: Which living beings are given special attention in the passage when mercy is described?
questions.answer: All living creatures are included, especially those that have just come into the world.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the way needs are provided?
questions.answer: It says their needs are delivered in a very orderly and careful way, with nothing left out.

questions.question: What does the passage say mercy does not do when caring for creatures?
questions.answer: It does not overlook any of their needs.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by saying mercy reaches individuals everywhere at the same moment?
questions.answer: It means Allah’s care is not limited to one place or one group, but extends to all at once.

questions.question: Why does this all-reaching care point to unity?
questions.answer: Because one perfectly ordered care covers everything, which shows one source is managing it.

questions.question: What comparison is made between the truth of Opening and the truth of Mercifulness?
questions.answer: Both are said to prove unity clearly; one does so through forming beings in order, and the other through caring for living things in order.

questions.question: What part of life in this world is highlighted as evidence of mercy?
questions.answer: The arrival of living beings into worldly life and the way they are provided for.

questions.question: Why does simultaneous care support the idea of oneness within unity?
questions.answer: Because many separate creatures are cared for through one all-encompassing mercy.

questions.question: What is the main subject of the marked passage?
questions.answer: It explains how divine mercy caring for all living things points to Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: According to the passage, what feature of all beings formed through Opening makes the proof very clear?
questions.answer: Their forms are made and spread out with regularity and order.

questions.question: In the passage, what quality of mercy makes it broad and far-reaching?
questions.answer: It includes everything and reaches all creatures.

questions.question: What kind of creatures are mentioned as entering the life of this world?
questions.answer: Animate beings, meaning living creatures.

questions.question: Which group among these living creatures is especially mentioned?
questions.answer: Those newly brought into life.

questions.question: What three qualities describe how they are cared for?
questions.answer: They are cared for with order, regularity, and complete provision.

questions.question: What can a reader infer from the statement that none of their needs are forgotten?
questions.answer: The care is full, aware, and exact, not careless or partial.

questions.question: How does the passage connect care for individuals with care for all?
questions.answer: It says each individual is reached, and this happens everywhere at the same time.

questions.question: In what way are these two truths alike?
questions.answer: Both serve as strong evidence for divine unity.

questions.question: What truth in the passage is said to embrace all things?
questions.answer: The truth of Mercifulness.

questions.question: What result comes from the ordered making of the forms of beings?
questions.answer: It gives a very obvious proof of unity.

questions.question: What action of mercy is emphasized toward living creatures?
questions.answer: Mercy raises and supports them when they come into worldly life.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the delivery of necessities?
questions.answer: It says necessities reach living beings in an organized and dependable way.

questions.question: How complete is this provision according to the passage?
questions.answer: It is complete enough that nothing needed is neglected.

questions.question: What does “everywhere at the same instant” help the reader understand?
questions.answer: That this mercy is universal and not limited by place.
